Rashi on Sukkah 15b:1:1.hebrew: והא אפשר לצמצם - קס"ד דהאי דקמתרץ בנכנס ויוצא, הכי מתרץ: כל כמותו בנכנס ויוצא הוא; סתמא הוא בנכנס ויוצא, דאין דרך לצמצם ולכוין כמותן ממש, לא פחות ולא יותר. ופרכינן: והא אם יתן דעתו לכך, אפשר לצמצם, וקתני מתניתין כמותן כשרה, והוה ליה פרוץ כעומד:
Rashi on Sukkah 15b:1:1.english: But isn’t it possible to be precise - It was initially assumed that the one who answered "entering and exiting" answered as follows: Any [instance of] "like them" is [a case where it] enters and exits; ordinarily it is [where it] enters and exits, as it is not common practice to calibrate precisely and align [the spaces to be] exactly like them, neither less nor more. And we object: But if he directs his attention to this, it is possible to calibrate precisely, and the Mishnah teaches [that if the space is] "like them," [the sukkah is] fit — and [in such a case] it would be [a situation of] breached equal to standing.

Rashi on Sukkah 15b:1:2.hebrew: ומשני אמר רבי אמי במעדיף - מתניתין לא אכשר במצמצם, אלא במעדיף ריוח שבינתים על רחב השפודין. וכמותן דקתני — בנכנס ויוצא:
Rashi on Sukkah 15b:1:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Rabbi Ami said: Where one extends - The Mishnah did not validate [the sukkah where one] is precise [in calibrating the spaces], but rather where one extends the space between them [to exceed] the width of the spits; and [as for] that which it teaches, "equal to them" — [it means where thatch of that size can] enter and exit [freely].

Rashi on Sukkah 15b:2:1.hebrew: רבא אמר - אפילו במצמצם. ואם היו נתונין השפודין שתי, נותנן לקנים של סכך ערב — דע"כ אם אינו נותן ראשי הקנים על שפודין, הרי הן נופלין לארץ. והלכך, הוה ליה כשר מרובה על הפסול ומבטלן:
Rashi on Sukkah 15b:2:1.english: Rava said - Even where [the space] is exact. And if the skewers were placed lengthwise, one places the reeds of the sechach widthwise — for perforce, if one does not place the ends of the reeds upon the skewers, they would fall to the ground; and therefore, the fit [roofing] is greater than the unfit, and nullifies them.

Rashi on Sukkah 15b:3:1.hebrew: בבלאי כלים - לקמן מפרש: במטלניות שאין בהן שלש על שלש. דאף על גב דהשתא לא מקבלי טומאה, כיון דמכלי אתו — גזור בה רבנן. ארוכות נמי, השתא לא מקבלי טומאה, דלא חזו למידי, אלא מכלי קאתו:
Rashi on Sukkah 15b:3:1.english: With worn vessels - Below, [the Gemara] explains [that this refers to] rags that do not have three by three [fingerbreadths] in them. For even though they do not contract ritual impurity now, since they came from a vessel, the Sages decreed regarding them. The long boards [of a bed] as well do not contract ritual impurity now, as they are not fit for anything, but rather they come from a vessel.

Rashi on Sukkah 15b:4:1.english: With a long [board] and two legs with it - And later [the Gemara] explains what they are fit for.

Rashi on Sukkah 15b:4:2.hebrew: קצרה - אותם אשר ברוחב המטה, לצד מראשותיה ומרגלותיה:
Rashi on Sukkah 15b:4:2.english: [A] short [board] - Those [boards] that are across the width of the bed, on the side of its head and its foot.

Tosafot on Sukkah 15b:1:1.hebrew: והא אפשר לצמצם - קא סלקא דעתך דהא דקמתרץ "בנכנס ויוצא", הכי קמתרץ: כל כמותו — בנכנס ויוצא הוא, דאין דרך לצמצם. "והא כו'", וקתני מתני' "כמותן כשרה", והוה ליה פרוץ כעומד. ומשני: "אמר ר' אמי במעדיף" — ומתני' לא אכשר במצומצמין; כך פי' בקונט'. וקשה, דאין זו סוגיא דהש"ס — שאינו אלא כמשיב דאינו חושש בקושיא שלו, דלעולם איירי בנכנס ויוצא! וי"ל: "במעדיף" — שמרבה בפסל עד שמכסה השפודים, ונמצא סכך כשר רבה על סכך פסול ומבטלו. ובענין זה פי' בקונטרס בדרבא: "אם היו נתונין שתי, נותנן ערב". ולהאי פירושא, קא משמע לן רבא דבמעדיף לא מהני, משום דזימנין דלאו אדעתיה לא ירבה בכשר; אבל כשמשנה להניח כעין שתי וערב, אי אפשר שלא ירבה. ומיהו קשה להאי פירושא, דאין דומה שיתבטל סכך פסול בכשר, אע"פ שהכשר רוב, כיון דאין מעורבין זה בזה וניכר כל אחד בפני עצמו — כמו שפי' בקונטרס ד"כשחבטן" דלעיל (סוכה דף ט:): שעירבן, ואינו ניכר הי ניהו פסול והי ניהו כשר. וגירסת ר"ת עיקר, דגרס: "והא אי אפשר לצמצם", כדפרישית. וניחא לפי גירסתו, דלא קיימא השתא רבי אמי ורבא לשנויי כמאן דאמר פרוץ כעומד אסור, דלכולהו קאמרינן הכא הך פירכא דאי אפשר לצמצם; אבל לגירסת הקונטרס, קיימי השתא לשנויי כמאן דאמר פרוץ כעומד אסור, והיינו דלא כהלכתא, דפרק קמא דעירובין (דף טז:) פסקינן הלכה כמאן דאמר מותר:
Tosafot on Sukkah 15b:1:1.english: "But isn’t it possible to be precise?" - One might think that what [Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua] answered — "[It refers to a space large enough for] entering and emerging" — he answered as follows: Whenever [the Mishnah says] "equal to them," it is [by default] entering and emerging, because it is not standard practice to be precise. "But [isn’t it possible to be precise?]" — and yet the Mishnah taught: "[if there is space between them] equal to them, it is fit," which means that breached equals standing [and the sukka is fit, contrary to Rav Huna]! And [the Gemara] answers: "Rabbi Ami said: Where one extends" — and the Mishnah did not validate [the sukka] when they are [precisely] calibrated. So it was explained in the Kuntres [Rashi]. And this is difficult, for this is not the [customary] style of the Talmud, as he is merely like one who responds [by showing] that he is unconcerned with his objection, [by asserting] that it is always dealing with [a space large enough for] entering and emerging! And one can say [instead: What does] "where one extends" [mean]? That one increases the fit roofing material until it covers the skewers, and thus the fit sekhakh is greater than the unfit sekhakh and nullifies it. And in this manner the Kuntres explained Rava's statement: "If they were placed lengthwise [warp], one places [the fit roofing] widthwise [woof]." And according to this interpretation, Rava teaches us that [merely] extending [the fit roofing lengthwise] is not effective, because at times he will not pay attention and will not provide an excess of fit [roofing]; but when he alters [the placement] to lay [them] in a warp-and-woof manner, it is impossible that he will not have an excess [of fit roofing]. However, this interpretation is difficult, for it is not plausible that unfit sekhakh would be nullified by fit [sekhakh], even though the fit [sekhakh] is the majority, since they are not mixed together and each one is distinguishable on its own — just as the Kuntres explained regarding [the case of] "where he beat them down" above (Sukkah 9b): that he mixed them together and it is not distinguishable which is unfit and which is fit. And the textual reading of Rabbeinu Tam is primary, who reads: "But isn’t it impossible to be precise?" — as I explained [above, on 15a]. And according to his reading, it works out well, for Rabbi Ami and Rava do not now stand to answer [specifically] according to the one who said that where breached equals standing it is forbidden; rather, according to all opinions we raise this objection here that it is impossible to be precise. Whereas according to the reading of the Kuntres, they stand now to answer [specifically] according to the one who said that where breached equals standing it is forbidden. And that is not in accordance with the halakha, for in the first chapter of Eruvin (16b) we rule that the halakha follows the one who said [that where breached equals standing] it is permitted.

Tosafot on Sukkah 15b:4:1.hebrew: בארוכה ושתי כרעים בקצרה ושתי כרעים - סוגיא דשמעתין כרבי נחמיה, דרבנן לא מטמאה בארוכה ושתי כרעים; דתנן במסכת כלים פרק י"ח (מ"ה): מטה שהיתה טמאה מדרס, ניטלה קצרה ושתי כרעים — טמאה; ארוכה ושתי כרעים — טהורה; ורבי נחמיה מטמא. ודוקא כשכל המטה קיימת וכולה של אדם אחד, שסופו לחזור ולחברה; אבל אם נאבד מקצתה, או של שני בני אדם — הואיל ואין סופן לחזור ולחברה טפי — אפילו איכא ארוכה ושתי כרעים, קצרה ושתי כרעים, טהורה; כדתנן במסכת כלים פרק י"ח (מ"ט), ובפרק שלשה שאכלו (ברכות דף נ:) מייתינן לה: מטה שנגנבה חציה או שאבדה חציה, חלקוה אחין או שותפין — טהורה; החזירוה — מקבלת טומאה מכאן ולהבא. והא דתנן התם: כרע שהיתה טמאה מדרס וחברה למטה שלה — טמאה; פירשה — היא טמאה מדרס והמטה מגע מדרס, אלמא דכרע לחודיה טמא — היינו לאחר שחברו למטה, חוזר לטומאה ישנה אפילו במטה טהורה; אבל כל זמן שלא חברו — טהורה, אע"פ שפירש ממטה טמאה:
Tosafot on Sukkah 15b:4:1.english: With a long [board] and two legs, with a short [board] and two legs - The sugya of our passage follows Rabbi Nechemya, for the Rabbis do not deem [it] impure in [the case of] a long [board] and two legs. As we learned in a mishna in tractate Keilim, chapter 18 (mishnah 5): "A bed that was impure with midras [impurity]: [if] a short [board] and two legs were removed, it is impure; [if] a long [board] and two legs [were removed], it is pure; and Rabbi Nechemya deems [it] impure." And [this ruling applies] specifically when the entire bed is intact and all of it belongs to one person, who will ultimately reassemble it; but if part of it was lost, or it belongs to two people, since they will not reassemble it anymore, even if there is a long [board] and two legs [or] a short [board] and two legs, it is pure. As we learned in a mishna in tractate Keilim, chapter 18 (mishnah 9), and in the chapter [entitled] "Sheloshah She-akhelu" (Berakhot 50b) we cite it: "A bed of which half was stolen or half was lost, [or which] brothers or partners divided, is pure; [if] they restored it, it is susceptible to impurity from here on." And that which we learned there: "A leg that was impure with midras [impurity] and one attached it to its bed, [the bed] is impure; [if] it separated, it is impure with midras [impurity] and the bed [is impure with] contact of midras" — which implies that a leg on its own is impure — that is [only] after one attached it to the bed, [in which case] it reverts to its previous impurity even in a pure bed; but as long as one did not attach it, it is pure, even though it separated from an impure bed.
